title: Sprint Planning — Feature Roadmap Q1 2024
author: Priya Sharma
content:
Attendees: Priya Sharma, Ravi Kumar, Ananya Nair, Dev Patel

Agenda: Q1 roadmap discussion

1. Authentication Module
   - Priya proposed adding OAuth2 social login support to the existing Auth module. This is a new capability currently only supporting email/password.
   - Decision: proposal accepted for Sprint 3 (starting Feb 5, 2024). Ravi Kumar assigned as owner.
   - Note: No implementation has started yet — this is approval only.

2. Data Export Feature
   - Dev Patel suggested adding CSV export functionality to the dashboard reports section.
   - No decision made. Needs design review first.
   - Ananya to schedule design review for January 22, 2024.

3. Notification Service
   - Existing email notification system to be renamed 'Comms Engine' to better reflect planned multi-channel support (email, SMS, push).
   - Rename approved by team. Effective immediately in documentation.

4. Search Module
   - Search module (currently called 'Basic Search') to be deprecated in Q2 2024.
   - Replacement: 'Advanced Search v2' using Elasticsearch. Priya to prepare spec by Jan 31, 2024.

Action items:
   - Ravi: begin OAuth2 design doc by Jan 20
   - Ananya: schedule data export design review
   - Priya: draft Advanced Search v2 spec

title: OAuth2 Social Login — Technical Specification
author: Ravi Kumar
content:
Feature: OAuth2 Social Login
Status: Approved (Jan 10, 2024 sprint planning meeting)
Owner: Ravi Kumar

## Overview
This specification covers adding Google and GitHub OAuth2 sign-in to the Authentication Module.

## Background
Currently the Authentication Module only supports email/password login. The OAuth2 Social Login feature was approved in the January 10 sprint planning session.

## Scope
- Google OAuth2 (mandatory)
- GitHub OAuth2 (mandatory)
- Apple Sign-In (proposed, pending security review)

## Implementation Plan
- Week 1 (Jan 29 - Feb 2): Backend OAuth2 endpoints
- Week 2 (Feb 5 - Feb 9): Frontend integration
- Week 3 (Feb 12 - Feb 16): Testing and QA
- Target completion: February 16, 2024

## Dependencies
- Auth Module v2.1 (already deployed)
- Google Cloud Console project setup (not yet done as of this writing)
- GitHub OAuth App registration (not yet done)

## Risks
- Apple Sign-In has NOT been approved yet — it remains a proposal requiring security review.

title: Auth Module — Release Notes v2.2
author: Ravi Kumar
content:
## Auth Module v2.2 — Released February 20, 2024

### New Features
- **OAuth2 Social Login** — SHIPPED. Google and GitHub OAuth2 sign-in are now live in production.
  Implementation completed February 18, 2024 (2 days ahead of schedule).
  GitHub: PR #447, #451 merged.

- Apple Sign-In: NOT included in this release. Still pending security review approval.
  (This was never approved — it remains a proposal.)

### Fixes
- Fixed token refresh race condition (issue #389)
- Session timeout corrected to 24 hours (was incorrectly set to 2 hours)

### Breaking Changes
- None

### Note on Comms Engine
The Notification Service has been fully renamed to Comms Engine across all documentation and code as of this release.

title: Architecture Decision Record — Search Module Deprecation
author: Priya Sharma
content:
ADR-007: Deprecation of Basic Search Module

Status: APPROVED
Date: February 1, 2024
Decision makers: Priya Sharma, Dev Patel

## Context
The Basic Search module was built in 2022 and does not support fuzzy search, filters, or real-time indexing.

## Decision
Basic Search will be deprecated and removed in Q2 2024 (target: April 30, 2024).
Advanced Search v2 (Elasticsearch-based) will replace it.

## Consequences
- Basic Search will enter maintenance-only mode immediately.
- All new search work targets Advanced Search v2.
- Advanced Search v2 spec was submitted by Priya Sharma on January 31, 2024.
- Advanced Search v2 is currently in development — NOT yet implemented as of this ADR date.

## Alternatives Rejected
- Upgrading Basic Search in-place: rejected due to architectural limitations.
- Using Algolia: rejected due to cost.
